entities.name: Query LpxC/FabZ
observations: 430 aa soluble protein; estimated molecular mass 47.6 kDa and theoretical pI 5.67.
Pfam detects an N-terminal LpxC domain at residues 5–272 and a C-terminal FabA-like dehydratase region at residues 299–421.
Full-length homologs Q8KBX0, Q7MXT8, and Q8A015 are reviewed bifunctional LpxC/FabZ proteins with 33–39% identity and approximately 99% query coverage.
Sequence-based assignment supports two activities: zinc-dependent UDP-3-O-acyl-N-acetylglucosamine deacetylation and beta-hydroxyacyl-ACP dehydration.
Exact acyl-chain specificity is not established from homology alone.

entities.name: LpxC
observations: UDP-3-O-acyl-N-acetylglucosamine deacetylase domain occupies approximately residues 1–302 in reference bifunctional proteins.
EC 3.5.1.108; zinc-dependent deacetylase activity in lipid A biosynthesis.

Reference active-site annotations include a proton donor near residue 287 and binding-site residues near 78, 260, and 264; positions are reference features and are not directly mapped experimentally to the query.

entities.name: FabZ
observations: Beta-hydroxyacyl-[acyl-carrier-protein] dehydratase domain occupies approximately residues 303–462 in reference bifunctional proteins.
EC 4.2.1.59; catalyzes dehydration of beta-hydroxyacyl-ACPs to trans-2-enoyl-ACPs.
Reference active-site feature occurs near residue 364; this is not a direct experimental mapping to the query sequence.

entities.name: UDP-3-O-acyl-N-acetylglucosamine deacetylation
observations: This is the committed deacetylation step in lipid A biosynthesis; the substrate acyl group is represented generically rather than proven to be myristoyl in the query.

entities.name: Beta-hydroxyacyl-ACP dehydration
observations: This reaction corresponds to FabZ activity in unsaturated fatty-acid biosynthesis.

entities.name: Zinc ion
observations: Reviewed homologs annotate Zn2+ as the cofactor for the LpxC deacetylase activity.

entities.name: Lipid A biosynthesis
observations: The LpxC reaction is part of lipid A biosynthesis, specifically the early committed deacetylation step; the FabZ reaction contributes to unsaturated fatty-acid biosynthesis.
